questions.q: What is Docker Hub, in terms of what this course has already been doing with it?
options: A build tool that compiles Dockerfiles
The default public registry that every docker pull in this course has quietly come from
A container orchestration platform like Kubernetes
A local cache that only stores images temporarily
questions.explain: Docker Hub is Docker's default registry -- every image pulled so far without specifying a different registry (node, ubuntu, postgres) came from it.

questions.q: Why does `docker tag northbridge/catalog:1.4 northbridgeretail/catalog:1.4` need to happen before `docker push`?
options: It compresses the image to reduce upload size
It connects the local image to a Hub namespace, since push only knows where to send an image based on its tag
It automatically logs you in to Docker Hub
It is not actually required -- docker push works on any local image name
questions.explain: A locally built image isn't tied to any registry until it's tagged with that registry's namespace. docker push reads the destination from the tag itself.

options: Creates a new Docker Hub account automatically
Authenticates the Docker CLI against a registry and stores a token so later push/pull commands don't re-prompt
Builds and tags an image in one step
Downloads every image in your private repositories
questions.explain: docker login authenticates once and caches credentials locally, so subsequent docker push and docker pull commands against that registry don't ask again.

questions.q: What is the real difference between a public and a private Docker Hub repository?
options: Public repositories are free; private repositories always cost money with no free tier at all
Public repositories appear in search and anyone can pull them; private repositories are invisible in search and restricted to accounts granted access
Private repositories can only be created by Docker employees
There is no functional difference, only a cosmetic label
questions.explain: Visibility controls discoverability and pull access: public repos are searchable and open to anyone, private repos are hidden and locked down to explicitly granted accounts.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge keep `northbridgeretail/catalog` and `northbridgeretail/checkout` as private repositories?
options: Private repositories build faster than public ones
Docker Hub requires all company-owned images to be private by default
They contain Northbridge's actual proprietary application code, not something meant for public pulling
Public repositories cannot be tagged with version numbers
questions.explain: Public repos are appropriate for open-source or shareable base images. Since these repos hold Northbridge's own product-catalog and checkout code, keeping them private restricts who can pull them.
